root_cause.text: Missing kfree() call in the error path when the device path length exceeds the output buffer size, causing allocated memory from kobject_get_path() to leak when the function returns -ENOSPC.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the kfree(dev_path) call from after the uverbs_copy_to() call to the end label, ensuring it executes in all exit paths including the error case. The original code only freed memory on the success path, but when dev_path_len exceeded out_len (causing -ENOSPC to be returned), the function would exit without freeing the memory allocated by kobject_get_path(). The patch also initializes dev_path to NULL to ensure safe kfree() even if allocation fails.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function MLX5_IB_METHOD_GET_DATA_DIRECT_SYSFS_PATH contains a memory leak in the error path. At line 25, `dev_path = kobject_get_path(...)` allocates memory. At line 32, when `dev_path_len > out_len`, the function returns `-ENOSPC` via the `goto end` statement at line 34. However, the `kfree(dev_path)` call at line 39 is only executed after the successful `uverbs_copy_to()` call at line 38. When the size check fails and `goto end` is executed, the code jumps directly to the `end:` label at line 41, skipping the `kfree(dev_path)` call. This leaves the allocated memory from `kobject_get_path()` unreleased, causing a memory leak when returning -ENOSPC.
